I took my dog to this clinic about two weeks ago because she didn’t seem normal to me. She was weaker than usual, and I felt something was wrong. We did blood tests and other checks, and the consultation was handled by a female veterinarian. At the time, we were informed that overall she was healthy—only slightly dehydrated and with low blood cells, so we followed the advice given.

However, about 10 days later, my dog was still weak and even started having nosebleeds. This made us very concerned, so we decided to visit another clinic for a second opinion. After running tests again, we were told that my dog was in a critical condition due to super low blood cells.

This experience was very upsetting. Looking back, I feel that the initial assessment and explanation may not have fully reflected the seriousness of her condition. With earlier clarity and guidance, the situation might have been addressed sooner.

As pet owners, we place a lot of trust in veterinary advice, so this was difficult to accept.

P.S. The staff and nurses were kind and took good care of my dog. However, the diagnosis and interpretation of the test results were disappointing and had a significant impact on our situation.

text: Professional doctor. 10 years of my good experience here with cats and dogs
Excellent care for my dog, thank you, and inexpensive too...
I made an appointment by phone, but when I arrived, the staff suggested I go somewhere else.

I waited for over an hour. I described the kitten's symptoms: lethargic, weak, and vomiting. The staff checked on it several times, and the last time, they held the kitten and checked its gums—they were pale. I thought they would do something or take it in for examination immediately because there was only one person ahead of me who was already being examined. But when they saw the pale gums, they said, "It's okay, it's still alright." I was confused; it was clearly very pale and the kitten was weak. Five minutes later, the kitten died in my hands. I walked over and said, "No need, I'm going home. It's gone." They immediately found an examination room, saying, "This room will do." I asked, "Is it really possible? It's already stopped breathing." When we went in, the female vet looked distressed. I admit, I was in a bad state when I arrived. I woke up to find the kitten lying weak on the floor, so I washed my face, brushed my teeth, and took it to the vet. If I had seen the vet from the moment I sat down, and the staff had checked on it, I think the kitten would have survived. After leaving the examination room, all the staff stood silently. This was the first and last time I'll ever go to this place.
